title: Decouple prefetch from admission; introduce per-tenant buffer grace periods for hosted GPU pools
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
Recent hosted GPU capacity exhaustion incidents have shown a pattern: aggressive prefetch logic inflates GPU pool admission signals, causing synchronized queue growth and amplification when autoscaler lag appears. Prefetch currently increments the same admission counters used for real client traffic, which masks actual headroom and makes the autoscaler and throttling subsystems react too late.

Goal:
Decouple prefetch (KV/prefix priming and model warm-up) from admission scoring and introduce a per-tenant buffer (grace period) that absorbs short-lived prefetch spikes without contributing to eviction/throttle signals. This reduces queue amplification, prevents unnecessary tenant throttling, and stabilizes autoscaler decisions during transient bursts.

Scope:
- Change admission path to tag and exclude prefetch-originated work from tenant admission credits.
- Add a configurable per-tenant soft buffer (grace tokens/time window) that temporarily tolerates small queue increases without triggering hard admission backpressure.
- Add metrics and dashboards to measure prefetch-induced admission noise, grace buffer utilization, and impact on scale decisions.
- Add integration tests and a staging experiment to validate behavior under synthetic prefetch-heavy workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Prefetch requests are no longer counted against tenant admission credits in the admission service and dispatcher
Per-tenant grace buffer exists and is configurable at runtime; default: 200ms grace window or 50 token buffer
Autoscaler uses adjusted headroom metrics that exclude prefetch-only transient load
No customer-facing increase in tail-latency or 5xxs observed during staging experiments with synthetic prefetch bursts
Dashboard panels show: prefetch vs client admission delta, grace buffer fill rate, adjusted headroom signal, and autoscaler decision timestamps
action_items: Implement admission tag for prefetch traffic in dispatcher (small change to request metadata)
Patch admission scoring to ignore tagged prefetch for immediate eviction/throttle counters
Implement per-tenant soft buffer store and enforcement with metrics emissions
Add feature flag to enable grace-buffers per-pool for controlled rollout
Create synthetic load job for staging that mimics prefetch-heavy client patterns
Run 72-hour staging experiment and collect dashboards and flamegraphs
If staging results are positive, create rollout plan with canary on 10% of pools, monitor for 48 hours before 50% expansion
notes: Observed root causes in recent incidents: (1) prefetch was indistinguishable from live traffic in admission path, (2) autoscaler hysteresis caused slow response to real load while prefetch inflated metrics, (3) tenant-level throttles were too aggressive during short bursts

Tradeoffs: ignoring prefetch entirely could hide pathological prefetch storms. Grace buffer chosen to allow short bursts but still surface sustained pressure. Buffer size and window are tunables that will be validated in staging.
Related work: this ticket complements ongoing KV-cache eviction improvements and adaptive autoscaler tuning (see dependencies).
If we find prefetch drivers are misbehaving, a subsequent ticket will quarantine offending clients and add rate limits to prefetch endpoints.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Sofia Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem review of 2026-03-08 capacity event. Attached initial experimental plan and sample metrics exported from the incident timeframe.

2026-03-11 — Amit Patel: ✅ Implemented admission tag prototype and local unit tests. Found a race with admission counters when requests are requeued; added atomic update in dispatcher. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/ENG-324501-prefetch-tag

2026-03-12 — Priya Rao (SRE): Staging cluster test shows prefetch tag reduces apparent admission utilization by ~35% during synthetic bursts. Observed autoscaler still delayed due to 30s smoothing window; propose adjusting autoscaler smoothing to use adjusted headroom metric.

2026-03-13 — Amit Patel: Added grace buffer implementation behind feature flag. Default configured small; submitted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/6578. Requesting review from runtime team.

2026-03-14 — Daniel Kim (Performance): Ran 6-hour staging experiment. Results: tail latency unchanged, 5xx reduced by 12% during bursts, grace buffer rarely exhausted at default settings. Recommend canary rollout to non-critical pools next week.
— Pending: schedule canary rollout, refine buffer defaults, and coordinate with Autoscaler team to incorporate adjusted headroom signal into scaling decisions.
